summary: Remote listener blocks in accept() instead of polling every 10 ms (shutdown wakes it with a self-connect); each IP holds at most one unauthenticated slot (a newer half-open connection from the same IP replaces the older one); the whole unauthenticated phase (TLS handshake through device authentication) has one 5 s budget that per-frame deadlines cannot extend; unauthenticated peers never occupy the half of max_connections reserved for authenticated connections. The handler promotes a connection with DeadlineSocket::authenticated().

validation_result.validator_half_open_flood: tests/remote_listener.rs half_open_flood_keeps_one_unauthenticated_slot_and_authenticated_clients_connect: 12 half-open TCP peers leave one unauthenticated slot; an established authenticated client survives and two more authenticate
validation_result.remaining_idle_source: owner thread 500 ms shutdown fallback (ZE-512), not the listener

notes: Deviation (owned path): src/host_pair.rs gets one call, stream.sock.authenticated()?, after a successful Authenticate; without it every device would stay under the 5 s unauthenticated budget. Pairing and revoke_status stay unauthenticated and must finish within the 5 s budget (handshake_timeout, unchanged default). Same-IP policy: newest-wins replacement rather than refusal, so a client behind the same address as stale or hostile half-open sockets (loopback, NAT, ssh -R) can still connect; a same-IP attacker can in turn displace a pending handshake, which it could equally do under refusal. Shutdown wakes accept by connecting to the bound address (loopback for a wildcard bind); if that connect fails the accept thread is left blocked rather than hanging shutdown (all connections are already closed). Accepted connection threads are now detached when finished instead of joined in the poll loop. Existing tests adjusted: the same-IP half-open test now asserts replacement, and the four-connection test's handler promotes after hello. No new unwrap/expect/panic in non-test code; no new unsafe; Arc<State> already existed.
